title: Constellations
examples: How do we know which stars belong together?
Are constellations always in the same place?
What is the difference between a star and a constellation?

explain.say: A constellation is a pattern of stars we see.
People named these patterns over many years.
Orion is a very famous constellation you might know.
The Plough, also called the Big Dipper, is another bright pattern.
Stars can be very far away or quite close to Earth.
In real life, we use constellations to tell time or tell stories.

faq.q: Are constellations the stars themselves, or are they just drawings?
faq.a: They are patterns we draw connecting the stars we see. The stars are real objects in space.

faq.q: Do constellations change shape when I look at them later?
faq.a: The patterns stay in the same place relative to each other. However, the Earth moves around the Sun.

faq.q: Why is Orion so famous compared to other constellations?
faq.a: Orion is very bright and easy to spot in the night sky. Many cultures have stories about the hunter.

faq.q: How can I tell if a star is close or far away just by looking?
faq.a: Generally, the closer a star is, the brighter it appears to us. However, brightness can also mean it is very large.
asks: How do I judge star distance?

faq.q: What is the difference between a star and a constellation?
faq.a: A star is a giant ball of burning gas. A constellation is the pattern formed by grouping several stars together.
asks: Is a constellation made of stars?
Are stars and constellations the same thing?

faq.q: Can I see constellations in the daytime?
faq.a: No, you need the darkness of night to see constellations clearly. The Sun's light is too bright.
asks: Do I need the moon to see them?

faq.q: What is the Plough really pointing to?
faq.a: The Plough pattern in the sky helps people find the North Star. This star helps guide travelers.
asks: What is the purpose of the Plough?

facts: Constellations are patterns of stars visible in the night sky.
Orion is a prominent constellation often seen in winter months.
The Plough pattern is also known as the Big Dipper in some regions.
The apparent brightness of a star can be affected by its distance.

quiz.say: What is the term for a recognizable pattern of stars?
quiz.why: A constellation is the specific name given to the pattern of stars.

wrong.0: A star is the burning object, not the pattern itself.
wrong.1: A galaxy is a huge collection of billions of stars, much larger than a pattern.
wrong.2: An orbit is the path something takes around another object.

quiz.say: If a star appears very faint, what might that suggest about its distance?

options.show: It is a different type of object.
options.say: It is a different type of object.

options.show: It might be very far away.
options.say: It might be very far away.

options.show: It is not a real star.
options.say: It is not a real star.

quiz.why: Distance is a major factor making stars appear dimmer to us.

wrong.0: Most faint objects we see are still stars, just distant ones.
wrong.2: Faintness does not mean the star is imaginary.
wrong.3: While clouds can block stars, faintness alone suggests distance.

quiz.say: Which constellation is known for having three bright stars in a line?
quiz.why: Orion is famous for its distinct belt of three stars.

wrong.0: The Pleiades are a cluster, but Orion is the named figure.
wrong.2: The Plough has a curved shape, not a straight belt.
wrong.3: Ursa Major is a different pattern entirely.
